description:
RE-FILED after tracker data loss (see docs/kopitiam-issues/). Originally filed by the op-yvj.4.5 agent.

Fixed-rule quadrature (trapezoid / Simpson / Gauss-Legendre over precomputed nodes) is the one kernel in ode::parallel whose arithmetic suits a GPU: no divergent control flow, uniform work per lane.

THE REAL BLOCKER IS NOT THE ARITHMETIC. The batched APIs take a caller-supplied Rust closure, and a WGSL kernel cannot call an arbitrary Rust Fn. Moving any of these kernels to the GPU means either restricting to expression forms the host can compile to WGSL, or shipping precomputed sample values instead of a callable. That design question should be settled before implementation.

SECOND BLOCKER: this container has NO GPU adapter -- compute.rs probe returns false -- so a GPU kernel written here would ship unexecuted and unverified. op-b4a.4.8 already tracks validating wgpu dispatch on real hardware workspace-wide.

This bead also blocks op-yvj.4.8 (hybrid co-execution), which cannot be built while every ComputeBackend::Gpu request resolves to a CPU path.
title: outram-foam-basic-lib: GPU fixed-rule quadrature -- the one GPU-shaped kernel in the hybrid epic

design:
Child epic of the nuclear refinery programme (bn op-upme).

**Fidelity target: Engineering model**

HTGR heat replaces or supplements refinery fired-heater duties.

Depends on the heat/steam/power ledger existing first -- there is nothing to
integrate against until units report duty **with temperature level**.

Scope: the intermediate loop interface; which duties are candidates at which
temperature; what remains fired; and the resulting change in flue-gas and CO2
source inventory (which is the actual claim being made for a nuclear refinery,
and must be demonstrated by the balances rather than asserted).

## Out of scope for this pass (programme-wide)

Do not: port DWSIM UI or graphical flowsheet objects; port CAPE-OPEN unless a
concrete backend requirement exists; reproduce .NET class architecture; make
DWSIM depend on Outram-FOAM; solve thousands of molecular species in the CDU;
implement molecular reconstruction before assay/pseudocomponent CDU works; call
a converged model validated without reference evidence; hide conservation
errors; push to `main`.
title: Refinery: HTGR process-heat integration

description: Add graded prism boundary layers at a wall patch (snappyHexMesh addLayers): compute per-wall-point inward normal, move the interior mesh's wall points inward by the total layer thickness, and fill the gap with N stacked prism cells per wall face (graded first_thickness * expansion^i). No hanging nodes (1:1 with wall faces). Needs a general assembler VolumeMesh::from_cell_faces (match shared faces by point-set) + cells_faces (invert owner/neighbour). New layers module: add_boundary_layers(mesh, patch, n, first_thickness, expansion). v1: a single closed wall patch. V&V: a box + N layers preserves EXACT volume (repartition), validate closed, cell count grows by N*n_wall_faces, the new outer wall sits at the original wall position, prism cells present.
title: cfmesh: prism boundary layers (near-wall inflation)

description:
Filed after hours (2026-08-11 23:55 +08) as a record only, per the CLAUDE.md
working-hours guardrail. No code was written and none should be until the next
active window.

## Ask

Give `outram-foam-basic-lib`'s numerical-math kernels an optional **hybrid
execution backend**: the same API can run serial, multi-CPU (rayon), or on the
GPU (wgpu), chosen at run time, with the serial CPU path always present as the
reference implementation.

Scope named by the maintainer:

- root finding
- golden-ratio (golden-section) search / 1-D minimisation
- matrix solutions (LDU + Krylov + dense)
- numerical integration
- numerical differentiation

## Why here

These are Layer 1-3 building blocks (`polynomial/`, `math/`, `matrix/`,
`krylov/`, `ldu_matrix/`, `ode/`), so every solver crate above
(`outram-foam-appbuilder-lib`, `outram-foam-turbulence-lib`, `tampines`,
GeN-Foam) inherits the acceleration without its own GPU code. The workspace
already has a wgpu precedent in `njoy-outram-park-fork` (Faddeeva/WMP kernels)
and `outram-mc-libs` (`op-u6s`, `op-9s8`), so the backend-enum + CPU-fallback
shape is established rather than novel.

## Constraints that bind this work

- **Hybrid means dispatch, not two APIs.** One public entry point per kernel;
  the backend is a parameter. The batch size / problem size decides whether GPU
  dispatch is worth the transfer, and that policy is explicit and documented,
  not hidden.
- **Enum dispatch, no trait objects, no `Box`, no lifetime params** (workspace
  Rust design rules). `ComputeBackend { Serial, CpuMulti, Gpu }`.
- **Android/Termux hard rule.** wgpu and any GPU-only test/example must be
  target-gated so `cargo check -p outram-foam-basic-lib --all-targets --target
  aarch64-linux-android` still passes and a native Termux build still works.
  Default features must stay Android-clean. Relates to epic `op-zfr`.
- **`uom` typing is not to be stripped** to get data onto the GPU. Convert at
  the buffer boundary and convert back; the public signature stays typed.
- **CPU is the oracle.** Every GPU kernel needs a parity gate against the
  serial CPU path with a stated tolerance, and the docs must carry both the
  methodology and the measured numbers (workspace V&V documentation rule). f32
  GPU accuracy is a known open question elsewhere in the workspace (`op-0nh`)
  — do not assume f64 on the GPU.
- **No human V&V is claimed** by any of this until the maintainer signs off.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-12: f32 GPU accuracy accepted for now, to be carried as a documented caveat in each kernel's docs and in the crate README rather than solved. See the note on op-yvj.4.7 for what the caveat must state. Also confirmed: the batched/lane-per-cell formulation is the right shape for these kernels -- batch N independent problems, keep single-problem solves serial.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
PRIOR-ART SCAN before briefing the remaining children, per the new CLAUDE.md hard rule 'Search the workspace before building anything' (9f36deb3a6, 2026-08-12). Done 2026-08-13. Three of the four remaining kernel beads would have produced duplicates if briefed as written.

op-yvj.4.3 (golden-section / 1-D minimisation) -- ALREADY EXISTS, working and in production use:
  crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/stagnation_point_outside_vle_ph_dome_multiphase.rs:67
  fn golden_section_max_g(...)  -- private, cited to Price & Robertson (2012), used for the HEM choked-flow energy-balance maximum and exercised by the Marviken tests.
  CORRECT SCOPE: generalise and batch THAT algorithm, do not write a second golden-section. If it is promoted out of the steam-tables crate, the choked-flow caller must keep working -- it is on a gated V&V path.

op-yvj.4.6 (numerical differentiation, finite differences + batched Jacobians) -- PARTIALLY EXISTS:
  crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/linalg.rs:183
  pub fn finite_difference_jacobian<F>(f: &mut F, x: &[f64], epsilon: f64) -> Option<Array2<f64>>
  Also crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/petroleum/lm.rs:162 jacobian_row, and finite-difference derivative helpers in tampines-steam-tables (speed_of_sound_eqm.rs:83 w_ps_eqm_region4_finite_diff_vol).
  CORRECT SCOPE: batch/dispatch the existing formulation. Note the epsilon choice and the Option-on-failure convention are already settled there; diverging from them would create the silent drift the rule warns about.

op-yvj.4.5 (numerical integration: batched quadrature + ODE ensembles) -- THE ODE HALF ALREADY EXISTS IN THIS CRATE:
  crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/ode/ = euler.rs, rkf45.rs, rosenbrock23.rs, integrator.rs
  CORRECT SCOPE: run ENSEMBLES of those existing integrators across ComputeBackend. Do NOT write new integrators.
  Quadrature: only crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/clean_energies/pem_fuel_cell.rs:934 pub fn simpson_integrate(y_vals, h) -- narrow (fixed-step Simpson over samples), so a general batched quadrature is genuinely new work, but it should match that signature's conventions where they overlap.

op-yvj.4.8 (hybrid co-execution) has no prior art found in-workspace and is genuinely new.

Precedent worth reusing rather than re-deriving, for whoever takes 4.7: the three landed kernels each measured their own crossover and they disagree by 1024x (256 root finding / 4096 LDU SpMV / 131072 field algebra / 262144 LDU vecops), and the root-finding one additionally depends on the CALLER'S residual cost. See the comments already on op-yvj.4.7.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Closed as GitHub #17. All 8 children done, and — checking scope rather than just the count — the children DID cover the epic's full named scope: root finding (.2), golden-section (.3), matrix solutions (.4), integration (.5), differentiation (.6), plus the dispatch layer (.1), gates (.7) and co-execution (.8).

BUT the epic's stated ambition is only PARTLY realised, and closing it should not be read as claiming otherwise.

The ask was 'the same API can run serial, multi-CPU, or on the GPU'. That is true for the data-parallel kernels — LDU SpMV, axpy, scale, dot, norm_l1, and closed-form linear/quadratic polynomial roots all have real WGSL kernels. It is NOT true, and cannot be through the current API, for four of the five named families: root finding (iterative), golden-section, integration, and differentiation all take their objective as a Rust closure, which cannot be shipped to a WGSL shader. Those kernels run serial and multi-CPU only.

That was not visible when the epic was written. It is a language boundary rather than unfinished work, and it is recorded once as the crate-wide rule in src/math/parallel/gpu.rs's module header. Whether to add a separate WGSL-objective API is now op-yvj.6, deliberately a decision rather than a task.

Second caveat: no GPU kernel is auto-selected. The crossover sweep found the GPU losing to CpuMulti by 5x-100x at every size from 4k to 4M lanes — but on an Intel iGPU via OpenGL against 32 CPU threads, which is close to the worst case. That measurement is re-opened as op-yvj.5 and could plausibly flip several kernels onto auto-select.

Follow-ups filed so nothing is lost: op-yvj.5 (re-measure on a discrete GPU), op-yvj.6 (WGSL-objective API decision), op-yvj.7 (async dispatch, unblocks co-execution forms 1 and 3), op-yvj.8 (characterise the quadratic kernel near a double root), op-x0n8 (six GpuContext implementations — consolidate?).

No human V&V is claimed for any of it.

title: outram-foam-basic-lib: hybrid wgpu/multi-CPU backend for the numerical-math kernels
